rationale: Every feasible run has large setup slack, limited at ss/100C/1.60V by a port path; the port-vs-reg2reg slack gap grows ~2.5 ns at 24-25 ns targets, so IO delays scale with the clock: use the tightest period_frac. Timing-driven placement separates results (TD runs T_eff 6.5-6.9 vs 8.2 without at similar targets). Within each group, slew-repair margin >=30% (~70 extra repair buffers) gave the best port delay. No congestion (DRC clears, wirelength ~ estimate); hold and slew/cap clean. Both failures used util 38-40, so pin low util. Keep best-run synthesis/RC (DELAY 3, orfs), and enable post-GRT timing and design repair so tight-clock re-runs repair accurately and hold the 0-pin bar.
